questions.question: Most heavy vehicles use the ____ method to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions need double clutching to change gears properly.

questions.question: Before inspecting your vehicle, look under it to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on an incline
Fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot
Whether the vehicle is on a decline

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle to check for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Leaks show that your vehicle has unsafe problems.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and makes a loud bang, the truck's handling is affected:

options.text: Only if the flat tire is at the front
Only if the truck is carrying a load

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay
questions.explanation: There is usually a short delay of a few seconds between hearing a tire fail and feeling the truck respond. This delay may make you think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS is not working, how should you brake?

options.text: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
questions.explanation: Without working ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as usual. Get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a small truck fire, you should:

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, feel them first to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed if you feel heat.

questions.question: When driving a tanker truck, you should:

options.text: Keep a larger distance between you and other vehicles
Let air out of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between you and other vehicles
questions.explanation: Sudden stops can cause the liquid inside to surge forward dangerously. Keep a larger distance from other vehicles so you can brake slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 cargo should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.correctAnswerText: A heater
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed in trailers carrying Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: Truck rollovers happen when:
questions.correctAnswerText: You turn too fast
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too quickly.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when doing something physical while driving
Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (like reaching for something) or mental (like chatting with a passenger). To avoid distracted driving, set radio stations before driving, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: How often must hazmat employees receive training and testing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once every three years
questions.explanation: All hazmat drivers must be trained on security risks and how to respond to threats. This training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle faster when going downhill. Before going downhill, choose a safe speed based on your vehicle's size and weight.

questions.question: Before driving a tank truck, you should:

options.text: Check pipes, connections, and hoses for leaks.
Make sure manhole covers do not have gaskets.
Make sure all valves are open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check pipes, connections, and hoses for leaks.
questions.explanation: The most important check on a tank truck is looking for leaks. Check all pipes, connections, and hoses, especially where they join together. Make sure manhole covers have gaskets and close properly.

questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly.
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is on fire, you should:

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Hope the fire goes out by itself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire needs special training and gear. Do not try to fight this type of fire yourself unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night.
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Fatigue-related crashes happen more often at night than at any other time.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be ready for them to move into your path. You can lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually until it reaches normal operating temperature.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks on a combination vehicle and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue.
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, connect matching glad hands together. Color coding helps drivers avoid mistakes. Service lines are usually blue, and emergency lines are usually red.

questions.question: When trailer wheels lock up:

options.text: The trailer tends to swing around.
The cab swings, but the trailer stays straight.
The tires will likely go flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer tends to swing around.
questions.explanation: A trailer can swing out and hit other vehicles if its wheels lock up. This happens more easily with lightly-loaded trailers.
